canonical_name: AMLR Regulation 2024/1624 — RTS/ITS Mandate
description: AMLR Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 mandates AMLA to develop 40+ regulatory technical standards (RTS) and implementing technical standards (ITS). These cover CDD, risk factors, beneficial ownership, remote onboarding, internal governance, and supervisory methodology. AMLA assumed EBA's AML/CFT mandate from 2025 for new mandates; transitional EBA standards remain in force until AMLA standards adopted.

canonical_name: RTS on Risk Factors and Simplified/Enhanced Due Diligence (Art.28/29/30 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS specifying: minimum risk factors for customer risk assessment; criteria for determining when simplified CDD (SDD) applies; circumstances requiring enhanced due diligence (EDD). Supersedes EBA/GL/2021/02. AMLA consultation: 2025-2026. Expected adoption: 2026-2027.

canonical_name: RTS on Standard Customer Due Diligence (Art.22 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS specifying the minimum standards for customer identification and verification: acceptable identity documents, verification methods (digital/physical), data elements required for natural persons/legal entities/trusts. Central for remote and digital onboarding. AMLA consultation: 2025. Expected: 2026.

canonical_name: RTS on Remote Customer Onboarding (Art.23 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS specifying technical requirements for non-face-to-face customer identification: acceptable remote identification methods (video ID, electronic identity schemes, qualified trust services), minimum assurance levels, liveness detection requirements, reliance on eIDAS. Builds on EBA/GL/2022/15 (remote onboarding).

canonical_name: RTS on Beneficial Ownership Verification (Art.50/51 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS on: methods for verifying beneficial ownership information; acceptable sources for verification (BO registers, company registries, public sources, commercial databases); verification of accuracy; procedures when BO verification is not possible. Key for complex structures (trusts, chains of companies).

canonical_name: RTS on Group-Wide AML/CFT Policies and Procedures (Art.15 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS specifying minimum requirements for group-wide AML/CFT policies: scope of group policies; information sharing within group; treatment of subsidiaries in third countries with divergent requirements; role of parent/subsidiary; policies covering branches and majority-owned subsidiaries.

canonical_name: RTS on EDD for High-Risk Third Countries (Art.35 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS specifying the enhanced due diligence measures obliged entities must apply when dealing with customers/transactions from FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdictions (FATF blacklist/greylist). Specifies which EDD measures are mandatory vs discretionary. AMLA will maintain EU HRTC list alongside FATF lists.

canonical_name: RTS on Correspondent Banking EDD (Art.38 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS specifying minimum EDD requirements for correspondent banking relationships: information to be collected from respondent bank; assessment methodology; minimum documentation; treatment of nested correspondent relationships and payable-through accounts; CBR risk scoring factors.

canonical_name: RTS on PEP Lists and Functions (Art.44 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS establishing: list of prominent public functions constituting PEP status at EU level; guidance on equivalent positions in third countries; criteria for national lists; timeframe for PEP status after leaving function (typically 12 months). Supersedes EBA guidance on PEP identification.

canonical_name: RTS on Transaction Monitoring (Art.59 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS on minimum requirements for transaction monitoring systems: risk-based scenario selection; review thresholds; alert management; periodic review of scenarios; automated vs manual monitoring; governance over TM system; documentation of monitoring methodology.

canonical_name: RTS on SAR Reporting Format (Art.69 AMLR)
description: Mandated RTS harmonising the format and content of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) across EU member states: minimum data fields, structured narrative, case classification codes, FIU reporting portal interface (goAML compatibility). Replaces divergent national SAR templates.

canonical_name: ITS on Supervisory Methodology (AMLA Regulation Art.37)
description: Mandated ITS establishing harmonised supervisory methodology for AML/CFT supervision across EU member states: supervisory risk assessment, inspection methodology, supervisory measures, supervisory convergence benchmarks. Forms basis for AMLA peer review and supervisory college outputs.

canonical_name: ITS on AML/CFT Data Reporting to AMLA (AMLA Regulation Art.11)
description: Mandated ITS specifying data and statistical information obliged entities and supervisors must report to AMLA's central AML/CFT database: SAR statistics, supervisory data, sectoral risk data. AMLA database will aggregate EU-wide AML data for risk analysis and supervisory convergence.

canonical_name: ITS on AMLA Direct Supervision Selection Methodology (AMLA Regulation Art.13)
description: Mandated ITS specifying criteria and methodology for selecting the ~40 obliged entities for AMLA direct supervision (DSEs). Criteria: cross-border activity, ML/TF risk profile, size, complexity, third-country exposure. AMLA first DSE selection cycle: 2025-2026.

canonical_name: AMLA Guidelines on Internal Governance (Art.9 AMLR)
description: Mandated guidelines on internal governance requirements for obliged entities: AML/CFT function structure; MLRO role and responsibilities; management body oversight; internal controls; audit arrangements; outsourcing governance. Supersedes EBA/GL/2021/05. AMLA consultation: 2026.

canonical_name: AMLA Guidelines on Staff Screening (Art.10 AMLR)
description: Mandated guidelines on staff screening requirements: background checks for AML-relevant roles; fit & proper assessment for MLRO; screening frequency; third-party screening; documentation standards.

canonical_name: Lifecycle Status: Consultation Period
description: RTS/ITS lifecycle stage: public consultation paper published by AMLA (or EBA for pre-AMLA mandates). Stakeholders (industry, NGOs, public) submit responses. Typical consultation period: 3 months. AMLA consults the AML/CFT Standing Committee. After consultation: AMLA reviews responses, publishes final draft.

canonical_name: Lifecycle Status: Final Draft Submitted to Commission
description: RTS/ITS lifecycle stage: AMLA Board adopts final draft RTS/ITS and submits to the European Commission for endorsement. Commission has 3 months to endorse (RTS) or adopt (ITS) without amendment, or 3 months to propose amendments. If Commission proposes amendments, conciliation procedure applies.

canonical_name: Lifecycle Status: Published in Official Journal (Legally Binding)
description: Final lifecycle stage: Commission-endorsed RTS published in the Official Journal of the EU. Becomes legally binding as an EU Regulation or Decision. Entry into force: typically 20 days after OJ publication. Application date may be deferred (e.g., 6-18 months after entry into force).

canonical_name: AMLA RTS/ITS × AMLR Article Cross-Reference
description: Each AMLA RTS/ITS implements a specific mandate in AMLR 2024/1624 or AMLA Regulation 2024/1620. Cross-referencing the technical standard to its enabling article is critical for compliance mapping: practitioners must identify when the underlying AMLR article applies from July 2027 (obliged entities) vs when the RTS defining detailed requirements is published.

canonical_name: AMLA RTS/ITS × EBA Transitional Standards
description: EBA AML/CFT guidelines and technical standards (e.g., EBA/GL/2021/02 Risk Factors, EBA/GL/2021/05 Governance) remain in force under AMLA Regulation Art.87 until replaced by equivalent AMLA standards. Supervised entities must comply with existing EBA standards and transition to AMLA standards as they are adopted. AMLA is expected to repeal and replace most EBA AML/CFT technical standards by 2028.
